answer: The USGS Ida high-water-mark file (data/raw/flood_ida/FilteredHWMs_NewYork.csv) has 159 marks (unique hwm_id, all event 312, all with valid lat/lon) at 83 distinct sites (site_no; site_id also gives 83). Marks per site: 1 to 3 (12 sites have one mark, 71 have more than one). By county: Queens 64, Kings 42, Bronx 24, Richmond 23, New York 6. The ProveIt truth catalog copy (usgs_hwm_ida_nyc) also has 159 records. The count of marks (159) is not the count of sites (83), so don't treat marks as independent locations.
traps_or_caveats: CSV line 1 is a citation, header is line 2; parsing from line 1 would mislabel columns (I skipped line 1; 161 physical lines = 1 citation + 1 header + 159 rows).
Marks are not sites: 159 marks at 83 sites; multiple marks per site are clustered, not independent.
7 marks have no height_above_gnd and 11 have height <= 0 ft, so depth statistics need care.
Heights are in feet (USGS), not meters.
Marks exist only where it flooded (presence-only), so they cannot measure false alarms without control points.
Some marks are interior/building marks; the keyword count (32) is a rough heuristic, not a verified classification.
All 159 are tagged hwm_environment=Riverine although this was pluvial flash flooding; label comes from the source.
Scope is the full five-borough file; the cached truth-catalog extract in a bbox query also returned 159, so no marks were dropped by that bbox.
